answer: Cross-Epoch Behavioural Fingerprint. Each identity's first emulated stack boot time is hashed as a kernel seed; every later epoch must reproduce the same boot timeline within a tight drift bound or the identity is dropped. Task selection patterns are logged against a basalt-weighted history vector, so a cloned agent cannot swap controllers without breaking the signature. Late-joining nodes pay a jetty penalty: they must replay all prior epochs' seed derivations before admission, costing roughly O(epochs) compute per clone.
